channel.title: Gas Morning Brief
channel.description: L'intelligence gazière en 7 cartes avant l'ouverture — pour traders commodity gaz

item.title: TTF stabilise près de €46, HH défend $2.7 avant catalyseurs US
item.description: Le gaz garde une asymétrie haussière malgré une apparence de range: les flux tiennent, mais la convexité reste chère là où le risque d’erreur est maximal. Le conseil retient un panier resserré de structures à risque borné et élimine les idées trop complexes ou redondantes. Exécution: discipline sur le sizing, protection optionnelle active sur Q3/Q4.

item.title: TTF Holds €44 as Ceasefire Dance Enters Decisive Phase — But War Premium Refuses to Die
item.description: After a month-long pause, the Gas Morning Brief returns to your screens. The gas market has evolved since our April 12 edition: the ceasefire has held (barely), Hormuz remains shut, TTF has drifted from €43 to €44, and the world has learned to live with a 00 oil price. But below the surface calm, the fundamentals are worsening. Storage is at 34%. Qatar is still offline. The MOU talks are fragile. This is not a market at peace — it's a market holding its breath. Today's edition: 8 cards, 24 trade ideas, and one message: the break is coming, and you need to be positioned before it does.

item.title: TTF steadies while HH range-trades ahead of US storage print
item.description: Le marché du gaz reste en régime binaire: un socle fondamental plus calme, mais une prime géopolitique toujours active. Le conseil valide majoritairement les structures convexes et les spreads définis en risque, avec discipline sur les ventes d’upside nue. En clair: rester tactique sur le spot, mais protégé sur les queues.

item.title: TTF Eases to €46.70 as Hormuz Fears Recede, HH Drifts to $2.77
item.description: Europe enters the critical summer injection campaign at a multi-year storage low while Hormuz remains locked in diplomatic stalemate. The triple threat of stalled LNG flows, a structural supply deficit, and Norwegian maintenance creates asymmetric upside risk — but the binary possibility of a sudden diplomatic breakthrough demands hedging. Position for the tail, respect the range.

item.title: TTF Surges 7% to Retake €49 as Geopolitical Risk Flares, HH Slips to $2.83
item.description: The gas market is walking a tightrope, caught between the bullish trio of Hormuz risk, a deep EU storage deficit, and upcoming Norwegian maintenance. The path of least resistance is higher, with any supply disruption likely to have an outsized impact on prices.

item.title: TTF Pulls Back to €45 as Hormuz Premium Unwinds, HH Firm at $2.83
item.description: Hormuz has moved from scenario to reality — 20% of global LNG is disrupted and Europe faces its toughest storage refill campaign in years at just 32% full. The triple threat of Hormuz, storage deficit, and Norway's hydro gap creates an asymmetric setup: the path of least resistance is higher for summer TTF. Trade the convexity — buy summer calls or strangles to position for a potential supply squeeze, while respecting the binary downside risk of a diplomatic breakthrough.

item.title: TTF Surges 5.6% to €47.10 on First Hormuz LNG Transit — HH Drifts Near $2.68
item.description: Hormuz Day 64 brings a potential inflection: the first LNG tanker to cross the strait since the war began. Yet one transit does not break a blockade — and Europe enters injection season at its lowest April storage since 2018. The council audited 18 trade ideas and retained 10: the core conviction is a barbell of calendar spreads and tail-risk calls, with unanimous support for the TTF Jun €55 call as the cheapest insurance in a binary market.
